A1.justification: Both PDFs provide readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–B. The shared token–expert affinity formulation and scheduling mechanisms establish continuity despite the change from Speculative MoE to Semantic Parallelism/Sem-MoE and substantial revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original throughput, latency, communication, clustering, and routing-prediction experiments in Section 5 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v4 reports original DP/TP serving measurements, communication and scheduling comparisons, and request/topic affinity analyses in Section 4 and Appendix A.

M1.justification: v1's cross-entropy optimization solver is replaced by alternating request scheduling and expert placement, including affinity scoring and expert swaps (Appendix B, Algorithm 1). v4 also introduces whole-request Attention-DP scheduling with device masking. The existing token-level TP lookup and shuffling procedure largely survives as Algorithm 3; the revision therefore goes beyond renaming.

E1.justification: The main serving workloads change from long-context, school-math, and code benchmark prompts in LongBench, GSM8K, and HumanEval to academic-subject and conversational prompts in MMLU, LMSYS-Chat-1M, and ShareGPT-Vicuna-unfiltered. LongBench remains in the retained Mixtral inter-layer affinity study, so it is not wholly removed.

E2.justification: v1 evaluates an integrated DeepSpeed-MoE baseline incorporating TED/Tutel optimizations and separately compares against SGLang. v4 instead compares against SGLang and MoETuner implemented within SGLang. The clustering comparison also drops METIS and 2D Balanced KMeans, replacing them with vanilla scheduling and MoETuner in Figure 5(b).

E3.justification: v4 replaces trace-sampled input/output lengths with fixed lengths and a 10–175 requests/s sweep, adds Attention-DP evaluation, and tests TP at 1 request/s with 256/512/1024-token inputs. TPOT and p90-TBT are replaced by E2E latency; the TP table reports p99 TTFT and median E2E latency. Main models change to DeepSeek-V2-Lite and Qwen3-30B-A3B, and main hardware evaluation is restricted to the fast server. The 20/80 profiling/evaluation split remains.

E4.justification: v1's component ablation comparing token shuffling alone with token shuffling plus expert grouping disappears. v4 adds a request-topic analysis using MMLU, Qwen3, and t-SNE (Appendix A.1). The inter-layer affinity, prediction-history, and PCIe communication microbenchmark analyses largely remain, rather than constituting new supplementary evidence.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. v4's p99 and median latency metrics describe request-latency distributions rather than uncertainty across repeated experiments.

E6.justification: The principal throughput and clustering results are replaced under changed models, workloads, comparators, and protocols. For example, v4 Table 1 newly reports Qwen3 TP p99 TTFT of 83.87 ms at input length 512, versus 101.86 ms for MoETuner and 104.76 ms for SGLang. These are not same-setting gains over v1. Appendix prediction results of 96.3% precision and 78.8% F1 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v1 Section 3.2's collective-communication derivations and stated savings ranges of 32–75% and 16–69% are removed. v4 retains a single all2all volume expression, changing alpha's definition from local to non-local activation for that expression, and adds a mathematical request-assignment rule. The original co-clustering objective and constraints largely remain.

C1.justification: The central contribution expands from speculative token shuffling and expert grouping for TP-based inference to joint scheduling of whole DP requests, TP tokens, and experts. The abstract, introduction, and conclusion replace cross-engine and heterogeneous-interconnect claims with SGLang DP/TP claims, including reported headline gains of 2.78x throughput and 24.9% latency reduction.

C2.justification: v1 explains stronger gains on slow interconnects and weaker grouping benefits for Mixtral's few experts; these applicability discussions disappear. v4 adds interpretations connecting request topics to expert affinity and explains large DP throughput gains through baseline queue buildup and rank synchronization. The qualification that conflicting affinities and limited memory can prevent 100% local activation remains.

D1.justification: v4 documents a SGLang request-scheduler extension and DeepEP integration. v1's descriptions of one-shot metadata/activation packing and deduplication are omitted. The approximately 5,000-line Python/Triton implementation, SRS/SAG implementation details, two-layer lookup history, and lookup-table memory example remain. Neither version provides a project code-release location.

R1.justification: Much of the training, serving, and offloading literature remains. v4 adds MoETuner, discusses EPLB and DeepEP, and updates model/dataset references. Its ExFlow comparison shifts from limited affinity modeling and top-1 support to model-only scheduling and allgather overhead, providing a focused revision of the closest-work positioning.

P1.justification: Extensive rewriting recasts the DeepSpeed-focused narrative around Semantic Parallelism, revises the abstract and contribution list, and reorganizes the method and experimental explanations around Attention-DP versus Attention-TP. Implementation becomes a methodology subsection, and terminology changes throughout; this is substantially more than a title update.

P2.justification: v4 switches the main text to a single-column layout, redraws workflow and scheduling examples, rebuilds benchmark figures, adds a TP results table and t-SNE panel, and combines communication and imbalance plots into Figure 5. Retained appendix panels are reformatted. Figure 6(b)'s revised DeepSeek-V2-Lite/ShareGPT caption conflicts with its retained DeepSeek-MoE-16B axis label.

improvement.justification: v4 adds substantive DP scheduling capability, relevant MoETuner comparisons, and request-semantic evidence. However, it removes v1's component ablation and slow-interconnect end-to-end validation, weakening attribution and applicability evidence. Reporting inconsistencies further complicate assessment: Table 1 implies a 17.7% Qwen3 latency reduction against the best baseline at 512 tokens, rather than the claimed 24.9%, and Figure 6(b) has conflicting model attribution. These substantive benefits and evidential losses do not establish a reliable net direction in overall quality.
